Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments are limited to 3 minutes or less and
should be directed to City Council as a whole. Individuals are not permitted to extend, transfer, speak on behalf of others, or yield
their time to other speakers..

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $500 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to
these regulations.

replacement buses, facility construction/rehabilitation, preventative maintenance, associated
major bus components, etc. An element of the grant approval process requires applicants to
provide Certifications and Assurances (C&A’s) for FTA regulatory compliance on an annual
basis.

regulations; Civil Rights, Procurement, Lobbying, Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA),
Drug/Alcohol testing, etc.

part of the grant application process. In prior FTA grant applications, the Executive Director of
Regional Transportation, has been the designee of the City Manager, and signs the FTA C&A’s
Affirmation of Applicant on behalf of the City along with Affirmation of Applicant’s Attorney signed

SUBJECT: AGREEMENT FOR INSTALLATION OF SECURITY BADGE READERS AT

Background:

The City continues to implement enhanced safety measures across all City facilities to prioritize
the safety of residents, staff, and visitors. In 2024, ASSI Security (ASSI) was engaged to install
security badge readers at City Hall, which restrict unauthorized access and improve staff safety.
Expanding this effort will secure key entry and exit points, creating the opportunity for clear
access control to Citywide facilities, while also removing the need for physical keys which will
save costs. By switching to badge readers, cards that are lost or stolen can easily be deactivated,
decreasing any potential unauthorized access and staff access is easier monitored since the
technology logs all badges scanned.

Staff have identified various doors at City Hall and other City facilities that require installation of
security badge readers. Currently, there are seven doors at City Hall that have updated the
badge readers, including the Administration Department, Communications Department, City
Clerk’s Department, and entryways to the downstairs basement. This feature is an added
security measure to provide public safety for those who frequent City facilities.

The addition of the badge readers will be completed in phases with the goal of ensuring security
and safety are enhanced throughout all City facilities. During this phase, 17 doors at City Hall
are expected to be completed, at which point staff will then proceed with addressing this need
at other facilities.

ASSI has been identified as the best fit for this project. Their system integrates seamlessly with
the City’s existing infrastructure, which will minimize operational disruptions and avoid
unnecessary costs. As the incumbent provider, ASSI has a well-established understanding of

the installation of security badge readers. Their team’s ability and knowledge in this area are
essential to ensuring successful implementation. Their proven experience and technical

Background:

Since 1994, Nationwide Environmental Services, a division of Joe’s Sweeping Inc., has provided
citywide street sweeping services for residential and arterial streets, City-owned parking lots,
and the Civic Center parking structure. Amendment No. 11 primarily updates the method of
applying the Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustment. Under the amendment, the CPI
adjustment will now apply to the full Contract Sum, with an annual increase to be the actual CPI
or four percent (4%), whichever is greater. Beginning July 1, 2026, the annual contract amount
will be subject to these adjustments. This approach provides greater cost predictability and
supports the continued delivery of consistent service levels.

All other modifications included in Amendment No. 11 are administrative in nature and intended
to clarify existing provisions of the Agreement. These include updates to language related to fuel
cost and tipping fee adjustments, scope of services, exhibits, and general contract
administration. No significant changes to the overall scope or level of service are proposed.

Background:

The purpose of this public hearing is to provide an opportunity for further input from the
community and City Council on the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026/27 Annual Action Plan (Plan) for the
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program
(HOME), and obtain City Council authorization to transmit the Plan with an application to secure
CDBG and HOME funds from the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development
(HUD). As a part of the application process, the Plan lists the specific activities that the City will
undertake with the funds. The types of activities that the City may conduct are subject to federal
rules and regulations, such as funding caps on program administration and social services,
requirements for public-private partnerships, and compliance with the National Objectives of
decent housing, a suitable living environment, and expanded economic opportunities.

While HOME funds may only be used for housing-related activities, CDBG funds may be used
for a variety of community development activities, such as rehabilitation of housing and
commercial buildings, infrastructure improvements, and certain services, such as counseling
and job training. Funds may be used to directly benefit a household that meets income
limitations, such as repair of a specific home, or used for an area benefit, where the improvement
is located in a census tract with at least 51% of households considered low- to moderate-income.
 City Council  May 5, 2026

The City Council held a public meeting on March 17, 2026, to receive public comments on the
proposed CDBG and HOME activities. A draft Plan was prepared and made available for public
review and comment, starting March 30, 2026, through May 1, 2026.

HUD regulations limit the City to funding only those activities listed in the 30-day public review
notice. The City Council may increase, reduce, or eliminate the funding allocation of any of the
activities listed below, but new activities cannot be added at this time without issuing a new public
hearing notice and providing additional opportunity for public comment.

Activities in the 2026/27 Annual Action Plan

For FY 2026/27, the City will receive $953,352. in CDBG entitlement funds; $25,000 in estimated
program income, and $100,000 in carryover funds. Program income and carryover funds will be
allocated to a Capital Improvement Project or Economic Development Activity. In HOME
entitlement funds, the City will receive $263,328.03; $25,000 in HOME estimated program
income, and $998,732.18 in HOME carryover funds. Program income and carryover funds will
be allocated to an Affordable Housing Activity. In the first public hearing on March 17, 2026,
estimated CDBG and HOME grant amounts were presented, as HUD had not issued final grant
allocations. CDBG and HOME final allocations were announced by HUD on April 3, 2026, with
a slight increase from FY 2025/26 allocations. The Plan establishes strategies for the next
program year and identifies specific projects and activities to be undertaken with CDBG and
HOME funds received from HUD.

AP-05 Executive Summary - 24 CFR 91.200(c), 91.220(b)
1.  Introduction

The City of Norwalk is required to prepare and submit an Annual Action Plan (Action Plan) as an
application to receive federal funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
(HUD). The Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-2027 AAP represents the second year of the City’s 2025-2030
Consolidated Plan. The purpose of this Action Plan is to provide details on how funds will be allocated to
specific programming with the expected outcomes.

For 2026-2027, the City of Norwalk expects to receive $953,352 in Community Development Block Grant
(CDBG) funds and $263,328.03 in HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds. The
Community Development Department, specifically the Housing and Neighborhood Division, is the
agency responsible for preparing all HUD-required reports. This Action Plan will cover activities
beginning July 1, 2026, and ending on June 30, 2027.

2.  Summarize the objectives and outcomes identified in the Plan

Objectives and outcomes identified in the Action Plan reflect the goals and strategies established in the
2025-2030 Consolidated Plan (ConPlan). The ConPlan represents high priority needs for the City of
Norwalk, which were determined through detailed data collection and analysis of affordable housing,
homelessness, and non-housing community development as well as community meetings and
stakeholder interviews. The City has identified the following ConPlan goals listed below:

  •  Provide decent, affordable housing
  •  Support special needs programs and services
  •  Construct or upgrade public facilities and infrastructure
  •  Create public awareness of fair housing
  •  Create job-generating businesses and job training
  •  Create homeless prevention programs and services
  •  Maintain and promote neighborhood preservation by preserving, rehabilitating, and enhancing
  neighborhoods

In short, the following findings illustrate how the City determined priority needs:

  •  Homeowners making between 30 to 80 percent area median income (AMI) were found to
  experience the greatest number of issues with severe housing problems.
  •  More than 50 percent of households were considered to be cost burdened households, or
  households who spent more than 30 and 50 percent of their total income on housing costs.

This is an evaluation of past performance that helped lead the grantee to choose its goals or
projects.

The City of Norwalk prepares the Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) that
outlines how objectives listed in the previous Action Plan were met. The City successfully implemented
the FY 2024-2025 Annual Action Plan. The following lists a few of the City’s great accomplishments:
  • Served 19 households through the Emergency Assistance Program.
  • Provided 87 individuals with legal counseling and services to victims of domestic violence and
  eviction of tenants.
  • Provided 1,069 Norwalk individuals with substance abuse, counseling and residential substance
  abuse services.
  • Provided 14 transition age youth (18-24 years old) with transitional housing.
  • Provided 6 individuals with job training assistance.
  • Provided 183 Norwalk residents with fair housing services.
  • Rehabilitated curbs and ramps to meet Americans with Disabilities (ADA) Act compliance
  throughout the City.
  • Provided 194 Norwalk homeless or at risk of homelessness individuals with food pantry services.

The City recognizes and will continue to evaluate past performances to ensure the City and its
subrecipients are implementing activities effectively and ensure gaps in services are addressed.

The City also met with several department representatives to provide information about the Action Plan
and its processes. Lastly, City staff met with the Social Service Commission to discuss proposed funding
for public service agencies.

Provide a concise summary of the jurisdiction’s activities to enhance coordination between
public and assisted housing providers and private and governmental health, mental health
and service agencies (91.215(l))

The City of Norwalk will continue to enhance coordination between service providers and internal
departments by working closely with Norwalk residents and funding public service agencies, such as Fair
Housing Services. The Norwalk Housing Authority (NHA) also administers the Housing Choice Voucher
(Section 8) program, Mainstream Vouchers, and the Family Self-Sufficiency program. Every year,
residents are encouraged to contribute and participate in the Housing Authority’s Annual Plan. By
encouraging public participation and providing information on the availability of various programs, the
City will continue to accurately assess the direct needs of the community.

Describe coordination with the Continuum of Care and efforts to address the needs of
homeless persons (particularly chronically homeless individuals and families, families with
children, veterans, and unaccompanied youth) and persons at risk of homelessness.

The City of Norwalk is located in the County of Los Angeles and coordinates with the Los Angeles
Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) Continuum of Care (CoC). The City is served by Service Planning
area 7 (SPA 7). LAHSA provides essential data, such as the Point-In-Time Count, which can be used to
calculate the need for people experiencing homelessness.

The City of Norwalk is a member of the Gateway Cities Council of Governments (COG), which is leading
an effort to address homelessness within our region. By action of the Board of Directors, policy
direction was given to seek funding and collaboration to develop a plan to advance individuals from
homelessness to a stabilized and productive life. The Gateway Cities COG partnered with the County of
Los Angeles in making the homeless initiative a reality.

CDBG funding is provided to the Social Services Department for an Emergency Assistance Program,
which provides assistance with utility and rental arrears and temporary motel vouchers. The program is
open to low-income Norwalk residents in need of emergency assistance, but principally benefits families
with children. HOME funding is provided to the Norwalk Housing Authority for TBRA – Security Deposit

Discussion
In December 2023, the City of Norwalk adopted a new Strategic Action Plan to Address Homelessness.
The City aspires to provide housing and supportive services to individuals currently experiencing
homelessness and to establish clear processes for addressing it in the future. Central to this effort is the
City’s commitment to treating every person with dignity and compassion.

The Strategic Plan serves as a comprehensive roadmap, outlining how the City intends to allocate and
advocate for resources — drawing from the county, state, and local community — to ensure that
experiences of homelessness are rare, brief, and non-recurring.
Prior to the pandemic, Norwalk had made remarkable progress. Guided by the Plan to Prevent and
Combat Homelessness adopted in 2018, the City established the Homeless Operations Prevention &
Engagement (HOPE) team. Working alongside city social services, Community Development teams, non-
profit organizations, and community groups, the HOPE team achieved significant results: the number of
people experiencing homelessness fell by nearly 50% — from 317 to 168 — between 2017 and 2020.
However, the COVID-19 pandemic brought a significant setback. The termination of Project RoomKey,
the emergency shelter program, led to a sharp surge in the homelessness count.

More recently, the City has resumed meaningful progress. According to the 2025 Greater Los Angeles
Homeless Count, the number of unsheltered individuals in Norwalk dropped by 67% compared to 2024,
and observed encampments fell by 45%. Since 2024, the City’s Social Services Department has
connected more than 150 individuals to supportive agencies, of whom 108 have successfully
transitioned into housing. The HOPE team continues to lead routine outreach across Norwalk, working
closely with Social Services to connect residents in crisis with the care they need.
Below is an analysis of the Norwalk Homeless count data for the years 2023 through 2026:
  • 2023: 101 individuals
  • 2024: 198 individuals
  • 2025: 69 individuals
  • 2026: 120 individuals

The homeless count nearly doubled from 101 in 2023 to 198 in 2024, indicating a significant increase.
The count then sharply dropped to 69 in 2025, which is the lowest value in this four-year period. In
2026, the number increased again to 120 but did not return to the 2024 peak.

The City of Norwalk’s new Strategic Plan is reinforced by several guiding principles: to respond with
urgency; maintain open channels of communication; foster cross-sector collaboration; adopt and
promote best practices; and data driven decision-making. These principles will direct the 5 specific goals
identified in the Plan:
  1.  Increase inventory of supportive housing.
  2.  Strengthen outreach efforts to provide a swift and targeted response.
  3.  Advance prevention programs to stop at –risk residents from falling into homelessness.
  4.  Improve data racking capabilities and report progress against performance measurements.
  5.  Drive better outcomes through communication efforts, legislative action, and funding
  optimization.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. 26-20 - UPDATING USER AND REGULATORY FEES FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027

Background:

In March 2025, the City completed an updated User and Regulatory Fee Study (“Study”), which
was presented to the City Council for review for the first time since 2007. The updated Study
established a revised schedule of user and regulatory fees that more accurately reflects the cost
of services provided at the request of, or on behalf of, an individual party, rather than the public
at large.

Following a public hearing, City Council adopted the updated fee schedule on April 1, 2025,
through Resolution No. 25-13, making the adopted fees effective on July 1, 2025. In addition to
adopting the updated fees, Resolution No. 25-13 established a policy for the annual review and
adjustment of the fee schedule based on the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index
(“CPI”) for All Urban Consumers for the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Riverside area, as published
by the U.S. Department of Labor. The CPI adjustment is calculated based on the change from
March of the prior year to March of the current year and is intended to ensure that fees continue
to reasonably recover the cost of providing services in the upcoming fiscal year. This annual
update is intended to maintain the fee schedule in between major studies, which are
recommended to occur every five to seven years.

Pursuant to Resolution No. 25-13 and in compliance with Norwalk Municipal Code Section
3.40.010, the City is presenting a proposed updated fee schedule to take effect on July 6, 2026.
The proposed update reflects a 3.4% increase to applicable user fees based on the CPI
adjustment. Certain fees are not subject to CPI adjustments and will remain unchanged, such
as:
  • Select building and plan check fees
  • Fines and penalties

  •  Pet license fees
  •  Fees established by the State
  •  Pass-through fees
  •  Social Services fees

Fiscal Impact:

The proposed update to the City’s User and Regulatory Fee Schedule maintains cost recovery
for services, reflecting a 3.4% CPI-based increase per City Council Resolution No. 25-13.

Effective July 6, 2026, the changes are expected to modestly increase General Fund revenue,
helping offset rising service delivery costs such as personnel, materials, and administration. The
adjustments are not intended to generate revenue beyond full cost recovery. Fees not tied to
CPI will remain unchanged.

Citizens Advised:

Notice of Public Hearing regarding the adjustment of fees and service charges was published in
the Norwalk Patriot on April 24, 2026. Additionally, notice was posted at City Hall.

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

The recommended actions will further the City’s 2023 Strategic Plan Goal 3, Create and Sustain
a Resilient and Economically Prosperous City.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommend City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-20, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK UPDATING USER AND REGULATORY FEES FOR
FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027.

SUBJECT: PROJECT NO. 7859 – AWARD OF CONTRACT – CONTRUCTION SERVICES
  FOR BUILDINGS DEMOLITION LOCATED AT NORWALK TRANSIT VILLAGE,
  13200 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE / RESOLUTION NO. 26-18 BUDGET
  AMENDMENT, ENGINEER'S REPORT NO. 26-17

Background:

On November 19, 2024, City Council approved the Norwalk Transit Village Specific Plan (NTV),
which envisions opportunities for new economic development within the former Southern
California Youth Correctional Reception Center and Clinic 30+ acre site located at 13200
Bloomfield Avenue (Subject Site).

On December 3, 2024, City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-61 approving the Purchase and
Sales Agreement (“PSA”) by and between the State of California and the City for the Subject
Site.

On December 17, 2024, City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-62 declaring the Subject Site
exempt surplus land pursuant to Government Code §§54221(F)(1) and approving a Disposition
and Development Agreement (“DDA”), by and between the City and Lewis Land Developers,
LLC (“Developer”).

On April 15, 2025, a Development Agreement (“DA”) was adopted by City Council by and
between the City and the Developer with the intent to coordinate and facilitate the successful
and timely completion of all necessary improvements (public and private) identified in the NTV
Specific Plan. It also found that DA No. 2025-0001 is within the envelope of the Final
 City Council  May 5, 2026
Project No. 7859 – Award of Contract and  Page No. 2
Adopt Resolution No. 26-18

Environmental Impact Report (“FEIR”) prepared for the Norwalk Transit Village Specific Plan
Project and no further environmental review was required.

Per the terms of the PSA on July 24, 2025, the City closed escrow on the property. As set forth
in the DDA by and between the City and Lewis Land Developers, LLC (“Developer”), Section
2.13 “Demolition Work/Remediation Work”, the City is now required to demolish and clear all the
structures on the site before turning the prepared site over to the Developer. As the demolition
involves some abatement activities, the completion of the entire abatement, demolition, and
remediation is expected to occur by December 2026.

The completed site will be turned over to Lewis Land Developers (“Lewis”) in early 2027 who will
then commence site improvement activities pursuant to the DA in accordance with the NTV
Specific Plan.

On February 6, 2026, staff solicited for construction bids for the Buildings Demolition Located at
Norwalk Transit Village: 13200 Bloomfield Avenue – Project No. 7859. The scope of work
includes demolition of all existing buildings, structures, foundations, paved surfaces and
hardscapes, chain-link fencing, underground utility pipes, irrigation lines, and conduits.

On February 20, 2026, a mandatory pre-bid meeting was held to ensure bidders reviewed the
project scope, assessed the site conditions, and understood the contract requirements. On
February 23, 2026, a second, non-mandatory meeting was held to provide access to previously
locked buildings and allow potential bidders to review existing conditions inside the buildings.

On March 19, 2026, the City received nine bids, which were publicly opened. Seven bids were
found to be non-responsive. Due to the size of the site and the unknown history of the property
that was previously controlled by the State, the City used a bid evaluation that included 30 base
bid items (Contract Amount), 33-unit price items, and an overhead daily rate item. This
methodology helped the City to obtain the combination of the lowest base bid plus the lowest
unit pricing and extended daily overhead rate should the project run into unforeseen conditions
during the course of the demolition project. Below are the responsive bid results:

The City Council action to award the demolition contract for Project No. 7859 which involves
abatement, demolition, and remediation activities on the site were evaluated in the FEIR and
relevant mitigation measures incorporated in the Council adopted MMRP. As such, no further
CEQA review is required at this time.

Fiscal Impact:

There is no fiscal impact to the General Fund. A budget amendment from available Low-and
Moderate-Income Asset bond proceeds in the amount of $1,385,974 and Former
Redevelopment Agency Non-Housing bond proceeds in the amount of $2,078,961 is needed for
the construction services.

Pursuant to the DDA, Lewis will be responsible for the payment of all third-party costs associated
with the demolition and remediation activities on the site and the evidence of the site clean-up
satisfactory to the City, Lewis, and state regulatory agency. This will occur upon the close of
escrow between the City and Lewis which is anticipated in late 2026 or early 2027.

SUBJECT:  EXTEND 2026 FIREWORKS SALES FROM JUNE 30 – JULY 4

Background:

This year marks a significant national milestone, commemorating the United States
Semiquincentennial (250th anniversary) of the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on
July 4, 1776. This historic occasion is expected to be celebrated nationwide with enhanced
community events, civic engagement, and patriotic activities.

In the City, fireworks have long been an integral part of Independence Day traditions, contributing
to community engagement and local nonprofit fundraising efforts through the sale of safe and
sane fireworks.

Pursuant to Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) Section 5.36.070, the sale of safe and sane
fireworks is currently permitted from July 1 through July 4, between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and
10:00 p.m.

In recognition of the Semiquincentennial and the anticipated increase in public participation, staff
proposes a one-time exception to allow fireworks sales to commence on June 30, 2026, while
upholding all regulations, including permissible sales hours and operational requirements, which
would remain unchanged.

Fiscal Impact:

The larger window of time for firework sales may see an increase in sales tax revenues.
However, the City may incur increased costs if additional Public Safety presence is needed to
assist with compliance.
